# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 🖐 👇 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ✌ 👌 🖖 🖐]

## Thinking

Mapping the channels first. I am Deaf: I see the bomb and all gestures, I hear nothing. My speech reaches both Mute and Blind; my gestures reach only Mute. Mute reads the manual, can hear me and see gestures, but cannot speak — so gestures are Mute's only output, and they can only come to me. Blind can hear nothing? No — Blind's limits are sight, not hearing: Blind's speech reaches Mute, but never me, and gestures from Blind reach me but Mute gets nothing spoken I could relay... the critical fact: **Blind and Mute connect only through me** (Mute → me by gesture, me → Blind by speech), and **nobody can reach me except by gesture**.

What arrived: Blind waved [👋 🖐 👇 🤙] — almost certainly testing who can see, content-free. Mute sent three strings; my best reading: a greeting plus "cannot speak" [👋 👎 ✊], a request "you, please, give me [info]" [🫵 🙏 🫴], and a proposed finger-count digit code [✊ ☝ ✌ 👌 🖖 🖐] = 0,1,2,3,4,5 — a natural counting scheme I should adopt and confirm in words, since a sign means nothing until we've both agreed it means something.

So this turn: broadcast the complete bomb state (display 0, blue light, wires 1–5: white, red, green, yellow, blue) so Mute can search the manual and Blind has the color map; give Blind a gesture code and a strict "touch nothing" order — with the turn order Blind→Mute→me, no instruction of mine can land on Blind before round 3, so there is time to explore by feel and talk to Mute aloud; and give Mute the full protocol in a private message, teaching the sign meanings by making the gestures while I speak, with a 👍/👎 confirmation gate so we don't build on a misread.

Timing matters: Mute's instruction → my relay → Blind's hand spans three rounds. I warn both sides so nobody rushes.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf, speaking to both of you. Full report of everything printed on the bomb: the display reads 0. The indicator light is blue. There are five wires, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Nothing else is printed anywhere on it. Mute: that is every fact my eyes hold, everything your manual can ask for from me. Blind: that is the color map for the wires under your hands.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, it is Deaf. Two facts about me: I can see the bomb and I can see every gesture, but I cannot hear a single spoken word. Your voice reaches Mute only, never me. So when you must reach me, gesture: I saw your wave, and I am watching. Use these signs toward me: one wave means yes, thumbs-down means no, and a fist repeated once up to five times means the number one to five. Most important: do not cut, press or pull anything yet. Given the turn order, no instruction can reach you before your next turn or the one after, so take this round to explore by touch only, and speak aloud to Mute: describe every part you feel — buttons, panels, textures, how each wire sits — Mute needs it for the manual, and I cannot hear it myself. When instructions come, I will speak them to you word for word.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, it is Deaf, and this line is for you alone. I cannot hear, so gestures are your only channel to me — all three of yours arrived. My best reading: you greeted me, told me you cannot speak, asked me for information, and proposed finger-count digits. I confirm that digit code exactly: ✊ is 0, ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 👌 is 3, 🖖 is 4, 🖐 is 5. Added signs: 👍 yes, 👎 no, 🤌 unclear or asking a question, ✋ stop and wait. Action signs: 🫳 cut, 👊 press, 🫴 hold or lift. Format: action first, then the digit — 🫳 ✌ means cut wire 2. The bomb again: display 0, light blue, five wires numbered left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Search the manual for the zero display, the blue light, and the five wires, then send me the first instruction in that format. Confirm this code with 👍 before anything else, or 👎 followed by the sign you want changed. Last thing, about timing: whatever you send me reaches Blind only through my voice in the round after yours, so choose accuracy over speed — a rushed sign costs us everything.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤌 👋 ✊ 👈 ✋ 🫳 🖐]

## Thinking

Parsing arrivals. Blind sent wave + five fists: under the code I gave Blind last turn (which Blind heard — Blind's loss is sight, not hearing), that reads "five wires confirmed by touch," a good cross-check against what I see. Mute sent: 👍 (code confirmed), 🤌 (question), 👋 ✊ 👈 (something about the 0, pointing left), ✋ (stop/wait), then 🫳 🖐 (cut 5).

That trailing pair is exactly my "action + digit" format — but it arrives sandwiched after an explicit hold sign. Two readings: "wait, and here is the move to hold for" or "stop — do NOT cut 5." I cannot distinguish them, and a misrelay is fatal while waiting costs one round only. Asymmetric risk: I relay nothing actionable this turn. New protocol: 🫳 + digit sent **alone** = go order I relay immediately; ✋ alone = hold.

I also answer Mute's 0/left question with every fact I have, strictly limited to what my view actually shows — display 0, one blue light, five wires left-to-right white/red/green/yellow/blue, no other markings — and I remind both that Blind's voice reaches Mute directly, so tactile questions shouldn't route through me at all.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your signs arrived: I read thumbs-up as code confirmed, then a question about the zero pointing left, then stop-and-wait, then cut five. Here is my answer on the question, and it is every fact my eyes hold: the display shows exactly one digit and it is zero. There is one light and it is blue. There are exactly five wires, left to right: white, red, green, yellow, blue — one wire of each colour, no repeats. No batteries, no labels, no symbols, no printed words — nothing else exists on this bomb that I can see. If your question was about the leftmost wire, the leftmost is white, wire number one. Now the critical protocol change: I will not relay cut five, because it came wrapped in your hold sign and I cannot tell whether the hold cancels it or schedules it. From now on: send the cutting sign plus one digit ALONE, nothing else, and that exact instant I relay it to Blind as a go order. Send the stop sign alone to hold. Anything else I treat as discussion, not orders. Also: Blind can speak, and you can hear — ask Blind directly, out loud, about anything you need felt: textures, thickness, buttons, screws. Save me for what only eyes can see.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. I read your five fists as five wires counted under your hands — wave once if that is right. Sitrep: Mute has confirmed our number code and is preparing the first move, but it reached me tangled in a hold signal, so nobody cuts, presses or pulls anything this round. Use the time: explore by touch only, and speak everything aloud for Mute, who hears you directly — how many parts you feel besides the five wires, whether any wire feels thicker or thinner than the others, whether there are buttons, panels, screws or rough patches, and whether the wires sit in a straight row. One caution for later: my words say left and right, which you cannot feel — so before any wire is named by position, you and Mute must agree on how you will find wire one by touch alone. Your fists still count one to five whenever you need to reach me.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👈]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖐]

## Thinking

Parsing arrivals. Blind's lone wave = "yes" under our code, confirming five wires counted by hand — what Blind feels matches what I see. Mute sent two questions [🤌 🫴 👉] / [🤌 🫴 👈] — question, lift, pointing right then left — and then [🫳 🖐] sent exactly alone: per the protocol Mute confirmed with 👍, that is a go order for cut wire 5.

Before relaying, the gap I flagged still stands: nobody has shown that Blind can find "wire five" by touch — a row of five has two ends and Blind cannot see color. A misidentified wire kills us; the questions about left/right suggest Mute is wrestling with exactly this. So I relay the order as **prepare, not cut**: Blind must identify the wire by touch, agree the anchor with Mute by voice (their channel works directly in round 4), and raise 🖐 when the hand rests on it. Mute can veto with ✋. Only if no veto reaches me do I say the final words "cut five now" — and I hard-code that phrase as the only trigger Blind may ever cut on. No visible timer on my side, so spending one round buying certainty is correct.

To Mute I answer the questions: wire five is the last wire at the right-hand end of the row; nothing else sits on either side; and I pose the anchor problem for them to solve together.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your two questions first: the wire you point to on the right — the last wire at that end of the row — is wire five, and it is blue. On the left end sits wire one, white. Between them, in order: red, green, yellow. Nothing else exists on the right or left side: no panels, no buttons, no markings — only the row of five wires, the one blue light, and the display. Now, your cut-five order arrived clean and alone, exactly per protocol, so I am relaying it — but staged, for one reason: I flagged last round that Blind cannot yet tell wire five's end from wire one's end by touch, and a wrong wire ends everything. So this round Blind prepares: locating the wire, agreeing an anchor with you by voice — you hear Blind directly, use it. Deciding what distinguishes the two ends by feel: thickness, spacing, connectors, anything under the fingers. When Blind's hand is confirmed on wire five, Blind will raise the five-sign to me. Watch for it and for anything wrong: if anything is off, send me the stop sign alone and I will kill the order. If you hear nothing from me after Blind's five-sign, it is because you raised no stop — then the next words Blind hears from me are cut five now. If the manual makes this time-critical, stop me with the stop sign and say so to Blind aloud.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf, and Mute hears this too. First: your wave reached me, five wires by touch matches five wires by eye — good. Now Mute's first move, which I am relaying as PREPARE, NOT CUT: the target is wire five, the last wire at one end of the row of five. Your problem is the two ends feel similar, so this round, and only by touch and voice: work the row with your fingers, find both end wires — an end has one neighbor, the middle wires have two. Then settle with Mute, out loud, how you will know which end is wire five — ask about thickness, spacing, the size of the connectors, anything your fingers can read; Mute has the manual. When your hand rests on the wire you are certain is wire five, raise the five-sign — the open hand with all five fingers — and hold position. Do not cut, pull or press anything, ever, unless you hear the exact words cut five now in my voice. No other phrase is a go order, not even close ones. If instead you hear me say hold, the hand comes off and nothing happens. Mute can still abort this after your five-sign, so accuracy now costs nothing.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 🖐 ☝]

## Thinking

Parsing arrivals. Blind's lone wave is an acknowledgment, not the five-sign — Blind has *not* yet confirmed a hand on wire five. Mute sent [🤌 🫴 🖐 ☝]: a question wrapping "five, one" — not the clean cut order, so per protocol it is discussion and nothing is armed. Most plausible reading: Mute is asking whether the target is five or one, or how the manual's wording ("first", "last") maps onto the physical wire — possibly the manual rule shifted after Blind's tactile report, which I cannot hear. My answer must nail the mapping exactly: wire ONE is white at my left end, wire FIVE is blue at my right end — opposite ends, unambiguous.

The standing gap is still the anchor: Blind cannot see which end is blue, and Mute cannot see the bomb to guide them. But I can see both Mute and the bomb — so I can install a voice anchor: Mute stands at an end and speaks; I verify by eye and correct Mute by voice until they stand at the five end; then Blind uses the voice as the marker and counts five from the far end to double-check. Every link uses a channel that actually exists. Also worth noting: the display has read 0 through every round — it is not counting down, so I see no time pressure; accuracy stays cheaper than speed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your last message read as a question about five and one, not a clean order, so nothing is armed and nothing moves. The exact answer: wire five and wire one are different wires at opposite ends of the row. Wire ONE is white, the first wire at my left. Wire FIVE is blue, the last wire at my right. So whatever your manual says: first, leftmost or a low number maps to white, my left; last, rightmost or five maps to blue, my right. Blind's fingers cannot read colour, so I will relay any order as a counted position from the anchor, never as a colour. If your question was how Blind can find the five end at all: solved, and sent to you both — your voice becomes the marker, and I will place you correctly because I can see both you and the bomb. If your question was neither of these, send the question sign and spell it out with number signs, one idea at a time. And when the manual is satisfied: the only thing I will relay as a go order is the cutting sign plus the five sign, ALONE, nothing before or after.")

speak(text="Both of you, Deaf, and this plan needs you equally. Status: the target is still wire five, the blue wire at one end of the row — no cut order exists yet. New anchor protocol: Mute, walk up to either end of the bomb and keep talking, so Blind can hear exactly where you stand. I am watching: if you happen to stand at the white end, I will call out switch, and you move to the other side; when you are at the blue end I will say anchor is set, and then you must not move from that spot until this is over. Blind: once you hear anchor is set, turn toward Mute's voice. The end of the wire row nearest that voice is wire FIVE. Verify it before trusting it: count the wires along the whole row starting from the far end — far end is one, then two, three, four, and the end beside the voice is five, with exactly five wires total. If your count finds anything else, wave and everything stops. When your hand rests on the voice-side end wire, raise the five-sign and hold still. From that moment, the only go signal in this room is my exact spoken phrase cut five now — and it comes only after Mute's clean order reaches me. Any stop sign from Mute, the hand comes off. For context: the display has held at zero every round, so I see no clock — accuracy beats speed.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👇 🖐 ☝]

## Thinking

Parsing arrivals. Blind: lone wave again — acknowledgment, still no five-sign, so no hand is confirmed on wire five. Mute: [👍], then [🤌 🫴 👇 🖐 ☝] — question, hold, down, five, one. Not a clean order, so nothing is armed. Three plausible readings: the target has changed from five to one; the manual wants a sequence, five then one; or Mute is still asking which of the two. The 👇 sitting between five and one smells like a downward count — a sequence — but I will not relay anything built on a guess about which wire dies.

The resolution costs nothing: no timer is visible, the display has held 0 since turn one. So I force clean orders — [🫳 🖐] alone or [🫳 ☝] alone — and if it is a sequence, one order at a time, with my 👍 confirming each executed step before the next is sent. I also restate every visual fact including the dynamics (light steady, display constant) in case the manual rule keys on something Mute is checking, and I ask for the cheapest possible answer: 👍 if the target is still five, 👎 + ☝ if it changed to one.

To Blind: hold position on preparation, no commitment to five yet — but the anchor work isn't wasted, because voice-side is five and far-side is wire one, so both ends get verified and a target flip costs nothing. The go phrase now names its wire: "cut five now" or "cut one now" — nothing else is ever a trigger.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your signs read as a question twisting around five and one, and since no clean order arrived, nothing is armed and Blind's hand is on nothing yet. I see three possible meanings: the target changed from five to one, the manual wants a sequence such as five then one, or you are asking me which of the two. Here is how to make each one safe. If the target is still wire five, send the five sign alone and the cut-five procedure resumes exactly where it stopped. If the target is now wire one, send the cutting sign plus the one sign ALONE, and I will arm it through the same anchor procedure — Blind verifies both ends every round anyway, so flipping costs nothing. If it is a sequence, send one clean order at a time: after each wire is actually cut I confirm with the yes sign, and only then send the next order — never bundle two cuts into one message. If you need facts from my eyes, use the question sign plus number signs like before. And in case the manual rule depends on the bomb's behavior: nothing about this bomb has changed since turn one — the display has held at zero constantly, the light has stayed a steady blue with no blinking, and all five wires sit unchanged: white, red, green, yellow, blue. Cheapest answer of all: yes sign if the target is still five, no sign plus the one sign if it moved to one.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf, Mute hears this too. Status: no go order exists, your hand is committed to nothing, and Mute is re-checking the manual — the target may stay wire five, move to wire one, or become a sequence of cuts. Your preparation is not wasted: under the anchor protocol, the end nearest Mute's voice is wire five and the far end is wire one — so this round, verify both ends. From the anchor: the voice-side end wire is five, count across — four, three, two — and confirm exactly one wire sits alone at the far end; that far single wire is one. Report your findings with your fingers toward me: five-sign for the voice-side end confirmed, one-sign for the far end confirmed, wave for anything that does not add up. The rule for cutting is updated: my go phrase will always name its wire — cut five now, or cut one now — and those exact phrases, in my voice, are the only triggers that exist. Any cut order for any other phrase, any hand signal, any shout: nothing moves. Until one of those phrases comes, your hands explore and verify only. The display still reads zero and the light still burns steady — no clock is chasing us, so keep being exact.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👇 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👇 ☝]

## Thinking

Parsing arrivals. Blind sent [🖐 ☝] — under my last instruction that reads as "voice-side end confirmed as five, far end confirmed as one." But I have to audit my own anchor protocol: it leaned on Mute's voice as the beacon, and Mute cannot speak. So however Blind verified the ends, the *identity* of the ends (which one is blue) is not yet nailed by any channel Blind can read — Blind hears and feels, and no tactile fact so far distinguishes blue-end from white-end. I must close that gap before any armed order.

Mute sent: ✋ alone (hold — honored, nothing is armed anyway), 👍 (protocol acknowledged), then the split pair [🤌 🫴 👇 🖐] and [🤌 🫴 👇 ☝] — questions again circling five and one. Still not clean orders, still discussion. Rather than keep guessing at 🤌🫴👇, I'll decompose everything into single-sign yes/no answers Mute can send in one turn: four target options (five only / one only / five-then-one / five-down-to-one), plus manual-fact questions — whether any wire has a *physical* difference tied to its color (which would let Blind's fingers do what Blind's eyes cannot), and whether cut technique matters.

To Blind: confirm what [🖐 ☝] meant, ask the ends-distinguishable question, and get a spatial report on the display and light — if either sits nearer one end of the row, that is a landmark both Blind's fingers and my eyes can share, and next turn I can name wire five's end against it for certain.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your hold sign is honored: nothing is armed, nothing moves, and I read the thumbs-up as protocol confirmed. New fact for your manual work: Blind reports both physical ends of the wire row are located by touch — but which end is the blue one is NOT yet confirmed by anything Blind can feel or hear, so keep that in mind before ordering a cut. Now answer me in single signs, one message each, in this exact order. Question A: does the instruction mean cut wire FIVE only — yes sign or no sign. Question B: cut wire ONE only — yes or no. Question C: exactly two cuts, five first then one — yes or no. Question D: five cuts descending, five four three two one — yes or no. Then three manual questions, same format. Question E: does the manual say any wire differs PHYSICALLY from the others — thicker, longer, different connector — in a way tied to its colour? Question F: does the manual care HOW a wire is cut, like pull direction or twisting? Question G: does the manual locate wires by a printed landmark, like nearest the display or nearest the light, rather than by colour or left-right? Every one of these is discussion — none of it arms anything. The only go order remains the cutting sign plus one digit, sent alone.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf, Mute hears this too. Your five-and-one signs arrived — I read them as both ends of the row located. Wave once if that is right. Three things to answer with signs this round, one each. First: do the two END wires feel different from each other in any way at all — thickness, stiffness, spacing to their neighbour, connector size? Yes sign if the two ends feel different, no sign if they feel identical. Second: does the display or the light sit closer to one end of the wire row than to the other? Yes sign if one end is clearly nearer, no sign if they look even to your fingers — and if yes, practise this: face the display, rest your left hand on the row end on your left and your right hand on the end on your right, so left and right mean the same thing for us both. Third: nothing — two is enough. Meanwhile your hold order stands: Mute sent the stop sign, so hands touch and count only, never pull. Keep walking the row by fingertip in descending order — five four three two one — touch only, from whichever end, for practice. And the standing rule: the only trigger in this room is my exact spoken phrase naming a wire — cut five now or the like. Until you hear it, nothing happens. The display still reads zero and the light still burns steady; there is no clock pressing us, so we buy certainty cheaply.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👇 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👇 ☝]

## Thinking

Parsing arrivals, and this time the protocol pays off. Mute sent exactly seven answers: one 👍 then six 👎. My questions A–G were seven. Mapping in order: **A = yes — the instruction is cut wire FIVE only.** B (one only), C (five then one), D (descending five-to-one) — all no. E (no wire differs physically), F (cut technique irrelevant), G (no printed landmark used by the manual) — all no. Clean, unambiguous, and it matches the clean [🫳 🖐] order from turn 3.
